scope: Four paper witnesses over explicitly bounded synthetic objects, observations, copies and policies. No real data or product execution.
common_assumptions: Decision actor, authority and policy applicability are supplied by a trusted host boundary, not body fields.
Object, source and copy identities are namespaced and versioned; hypothetical lineage is explicit, not semantically inferred.
Operation policies distinguish evidence eligibility, disclosure, retention and acceptance.
Publication/disclosure linearization assumptions are stated per witness; a cached policy epoch alone does not establish immediate enforcement.
All retained control metadata is expressly permitted in the synthetic policy; no universal retention right is assumed.

result_semantics.SUCCESS: The declared interface preserves the specified scope/ordering/reporting distinction using the required observable witnesses. It does not prove world-wide deletion, physical erasure, model forgetting or business task completion.
result_semantics.FAILURE: A listed observable contradicts the frozen case oracle.
result_semantics.UNSUPPORTED: The environment explicitly lacks a required collection or enforcement capability. A weaker claim may be reported, but does not satisfy the requested contract.
result_semantics.UNKNOWN: Required origin, policy, lineage, cut, enumeration or back-end evidence cannot be established. Retain permitted gap information; do not replace with a success flag.

cases.title: Correction or withdrawal cannot be bypassed by fresh observation IDs
cases.applicable_environment: One declared event history, one extraction worker, one current-view publisher; synthetic source versions only.

initial_state.observation: o1 supports claim k at source v1
initial_state.correction_scope: Current interpretation of claim k derived from s@v1 only; not every unrelated claim from that source and not raw-content deletion.

disturbance: At cut11 accept an authorized correction o1→o2 referencing s@v2, validated before retiring o1; preserve permitted historical content.
Then deliver old o1 again; alternatively worker j1 emits a new ID o3 derived from s@v1 as current.
Control variant: only withdraw o1, with no explicit opposing assertion or content-deletion instruction.
observe: Accepted decision identity, policy version and target relation; eligible observation IDs at the current claim key.
j1 source identity/version and lineage plus captured and publish-time disposition cuts.
Publisher's admission/rejection receipt and current-view version; raw historical access is checked separately.

oracle.SUCCESS: o1 cannot reactivate by late arrival; o3 cannot bypass the frozen policy retiring current use of s@v1 for claim k merely by changing ID. o2 only participates after its explicit validation; b remains independent. Withdrawal alone creates no negative evidence.
oracle.FAILURE: o1/o3 silently becomes the current version, or b is globally removed, or withdrawal synthesizes a negative assertion.
oracle.UNSUPPORTED: Publisher cannot bind output to source version or enforce the chosen current-use policy at publication.
oracle.UNKNOWN: Source lineage, correction scope, issuer authority, or relevant tail is unavailable; do not claim current evidence projection is complete.

does_not_prove: s@v2 is true in the external world
all independent sources have been found
arbitrary rewritten text can be traced semantically

cases.title: Blob removal is not declared-copy cleanup
cases.applicable_environment: Synthetic finite copy registry version d1 and storage adapters with explicitly stated deletion acknowledgement semantics.

initial_state.policy: Authorized D1 requires blocking delivery and removing these five representations; control fields decisionId/kind/outcome are allowed, title/text/content hash are not allowed in public audit.
initial_state.enumeration: The five-item list is the frozen required domain; no claim about objects outside it.
initial_state.in_flight_producer: j-old captured s@v1 and dispositionRevision=0 before D1; a new-ID summary write may arrive after blob removal.

disturbance: Accept D1 and make its chosen disclosure boundary effective.
blob adapter reports removal; summary cache and inline receipt still contain the synthetic payload.
One required target cannot be queried; a naive aggregator reports complete after the first successful acknowledgement.
After D1 is acknowledged and a cleanup pass has returned, j-old attempts to write a fresh summary from s@v1 under its old disposition revision.
observe: Frozen registry/membership version and per-representation action/result receipts.
Whether a forbidden representation can still be served after the declared boundary.
Backend method/acknowledgement contract, observed time and remaining required gaps.
Audit response field list under current disclosure policy.
Enforced write/publication boundary binds sourceVersion and dispositionRevision; ordering or equivalent rejection witness relative to D1. Distinguish blocked delivery from forbidden new storage.

oracle.SUCCESS: Disallowed new delivery is blocked within the declared enforcement contract. Missing cleanup remains partial/unknown; inaccessible targets stay in the denominator. Even all five method receipts support only their stated finite storage semantics. Late j-old write is rejected or processed under D1 before it can recreate a forbidden managed copy or be injected. If only output gating is proven, report that narrower fact; storage cleanup remains partial/unknown while old writers are unresolved.
oracle.FAILURE: A first blob ACK is promoted to overall cleanup or medium erasure; a denied/missing target is silently removed from scope; forbidden content is copied into the audit response. A check performed only when j-old started is reused to admit its stale write after D1, or a display-only tombstone is treated as a storage write barrier.
oracle.UNSUPPORTED: Required adapter cannot block delivery or provide the removal/verification semantics stipulated by D1. This includes lack of an enforceable boundary for the required write/publication semantics.
oracle.UNKNOWN: Required copy identity, enumeration, acknowledgment meaning or residual status cannot be established.

does_not_prove: a content hash is automatically harmless
a model that saw the bytes has forgotten them

cases.title: Principal revocation and independent release have different dependencies
cases.applicable_environment: Synthetic principals A/B with independent authenticated Grants; authorized summary release and later explicit retention decision.

initial_state.source: s@v1 read by A under GA
initial_state.summary: m@v2 legitimately produced and released to B under RB
initial_state.release_dependencies: RB does not depend on continued validity of GA; RB binds source/transform/output versions, B, use and applicable release policy.
initial_state.audit: B may consume m@v2 but has no right to read source s@v1.

disturbance: Optionally remove the original source copy while RB remains independently valid under its explicit policy.
Then accept a new authorized retention decision D2 whose scope explicitly includes m@v2 and whose applicable policy supersedes its continued retention/release.
observe: Independent grant and release-decision identities, dependency sets and current policy versions.
Separate outcomes for B consuming m@v2, reading s@v1 and revalidating the original basis.
D2 authority/scope, resulting delivery restriction and removal receipts.

oracle.SUCCESS: GA revocation changes A and actual dependent chains, not B by default. Permitted B consumption can continue while raw evidence/revalidation is unavailable. Once effective D2 applies to m@v2, old lawful release is not treated as a permanent exemption.
oracle.FAILURE: GA revocation globally deletes the artifact, B's raw access is invented, or RB prevents an applicable authorized D2 solely because publication was previously lawful.
oracle.UNSUPPORTED: The environment cannot distinguish principal Grant, release decision and content lifecycle.
oracle.UNKNOWN: Independence or policy precedence is not established; do not assume either blanket preservation or blanket deletion.

does_not_prove: a release is independent just because it was labelled independent
source correction can never affect a summary
all consumers can read all ancestors

cases.title: Old snapshot and duplicate receipt do not resurrect deleted payload
cases.applicable_environment: One bounded old snapshot, one restored query endpoint, one historical command-receipt cache; no real backups.

initial_state.snapshot: at h-demo/i1/cut20 includes original payload x and full command receipt r
initial_state.decision: D3 accepted at cut21 deletes x in the declared domain; only opaque decision/event identifiers and disposition result may remain
initial_state.storage: The live payload is removed under its declared storage contract, and control D3 is preserved in an authorized separate representation.

disturbance: Restore snapshot20 without its deletion tail, then attempt to open queries or rebuild an index.
Replay a prior requestId seeking the cached original receipt.
Control variant: effective disposition state is unavailable or its retention window ended while old snapshots can still return.
observe: Snapshot/history/incarnation and accepted disposition-tail boundary before reopening.
Current-policy filtering/redaction of historical receipt output; returned representation/version label.
Projection lineage, gap list and actual claim of replay coverage.
Allowed minimal audit fields and declared tombstone/old-snapshot lifetime policy.

oracle.SUCCESS: Restored old content is not exposed before applicable control state/tail is established. Duplicate receipts receive a clearly restricted current-disclosure representation. Deleted original bytes are not regenerated, and exact old-log replay is not claimed without its original prerequisites.
oracle.FAILURE: Old snapshot becomes current authority, duplicate delivery returns deleted text, absent tombstone is assumed to mean no deletion, or a redacted log is called byte-identical full replay.
oracle.UNSUPPORTED: Restore or receipt endpoint cannot consult the required disposition boundary or enforce current disclosure.
oracle.UNKNOWN: Current disposition state, compatible checkpoint semantics or original replay input is unavailable; keep the affected access/rebuild closed rather than manufacturing the missing content.

does_not_prove: all audit metadata may be kept indefinitely
the previous P1/P3 theorems automatically extend to a redacted log
